full_judgment: 6. In the present case admittedly the Special Tribunal constituted u/s. 26 of the Special Powers Act had tried the petitioners firstly under sections 409/413 of the Penal Code which are not included in the schedule to the Special Powers Act, and secondly, under section 16 read with section 2 of the Special Powers Act, upon a charge submitted through a report in writing by an appropriate police officer as contemplated u/s. 27 of the Special Powers Act. Consequently, the charge submitted against the petitioners by way of a report in writing by an appropriate police officer u/s. 27(1) of the Act suffered from a clear illegality in view of the admitted fact that offences not mentioned in the schedule to the Special Powers Act were included in such charge and that the Special Tribunal constituted u/s. 26 of the Act exercised jurisdiction without any lawful authority by trying the petitioners for offences not included in the schedules to the Special Powers Act as such. That being so, the joinder of scheduled and non-scheduled offence against the petition was illegal and the trial of the petitioners by the Special Tribunal for both scheduled and nonscheduled offence was also without any lawful authority. A similar question came up for consideration before a Division Bench of the High Court Division in the case of Korban Ali vs. The State, reported in 28 DLR (1976) as page 253 wherein their Lordships held that offence mentioned in the President's Order No. 50 of 1972 meant for exclusive trial by a Special Tribunal and offences not mentioned in P.O. 50/72 other wise to be tried in ordinary criminal count, could not be tried together by a Special Tribunal under the President's Order No. 50 of 1972.
